title: Amemiya 2019 foot-sole PPS, Experiment 2
citation: Amemiya, T., Ikei, Y., & Kitazaki, M. (2019). Remapping peripersonal space by using foot-sole vibrations without any body movement. Psychological Science, 30(10), 1522–1532.
notes: Software timing preview with a generated chest-target waveform and procedural audio. Figure 1b supplies the preview offsets. A participant session requires the exact recordings, independent conditioning outputs, baseline allocation and calibrated hardware timing.

reference_parameters.condition_factor: Body site receiving the same walking waveform

conditioning_conditions.label: Walking-sound vibration at the forearms
conditioning_conditions.site: Left and right proximal forearms near the elbows

condition_stimuli.site_waveform_rule: Use the same walking-sound waveform at the two sites.
condition_stimuli.individual_forearm_intensity: Before the main experiment use a subjective staircase to match each participant’s forearm intensity to their own sole sensation. Confirm the match in practice and record the participant-specific setting. The reported mean and SD describe the sample. The staircase step size, reversal rule, stopping criterion and physical gain are unreported.

auditory_stimulus.signal: White noise emitted from a loudspeaker moved toward a binaural dummy head on a handcart

figure_derived_preview_timing.derivation: Compare the four signed timing marks in Figure 1b with the shared 0–6 s waveform axis. The reference is graphical. The executable preview rounds each mark to the nearest 10 ms.

tactile_target.actuator: Acouve Vp216 voice coil on a neck strap

participant_setup.posture: Sit with the head still, the gaze on the frontal fixation cross, and the right hand ready at the numeric keyboard.
participant_setup.mounts: Use the neckstrap to position the chest coil over the manubrium. Remove shoes and position the heel coils in slippers. For forearm blocks position the two conditioning coils on the proximal forearms near the elbows.
participant_setup.chest_perceptibility_check: Confirm that the participant can feel the chest target on practice trials. The article gives no numerical chest drive level or staircase.
participant_setup.source: Published article, pp. 1523–1525, Participants, Stimuli and apparatus, and Procedure.

response.additional_offline_exclusion: Outside two standard deviations from individual mean for each sound location

baseline.target: Chest vibration at the same four delays on target-present trials
baseline.analysis: Subtract the baseline mean RT at the matching delay

blocks_and_repetitions.reported_condition_order: Modified Latin square across participants followed by the reverse order

auxiliary_procedures.name: Pre-task forearm-to-heel vibration intensity matching
auxiliary_procedures.method: Adjust each participant’s forearm vibration to match perceived heel vibration by staircase. Confirm in practice.

auxiliary_procedures.name: Post-task sound localization
auxiliary_procedures.response: Enter perceived sound distance on a 1–100 scale using keys.

auxiliary_procedures.name: Post-task walking sensation
auxiliary_procedures.response: Rate the sensation of walking during conditioning using the numeric keyboard.
auxiliary_procedures.order: Pseudorandom conditions, with task order counterbalanced against localization.

preview_scope.runtime_mode: Software timing inspection of active trials only

chest_marker_waveform.waveform: Generated sine with 200 Hz carrier and 100 ms duration as reported for the chest target and illustrated in Figure 1b.
chest_marker_waveform.amplitude_provenance: Toolkit software default. Physical drive and on-skin vibration require measurement.
chest_marker_waveform.source_scope: The figure indicates the carrier shape, while physical amplitude, gate ramps and delivered waveform remain unknown.

preview_scope.auditory_rendering: Procedural continuous white noise along a virtual approach at the reported velocity. The figure-derived preview uses a 5 s approach with a 1 cm near endpoint and 1 s tail. Those endpoints and the inverse-square setting describe a preview reconstruction.
preview_scope.catch_pool: The scaffold uses 20% no-chest rows within each active condition. The original catch allocation by condition and block is unknown.
preview_scope.baseline: The published comparison used constant-level white noise with the same four target delays and no conditioning. The software timing preview excludes baseline trials because their exact allocation and original audio are unresolved.
preview_scope.conditioning_and_blocks: Condition labels identify the paper’s intended outputs. The toolkit distributes the illustrated paired and catch pool across equal software blocks. These mix condition labels and keep block audio within the preparation limit. The condition waveforms and mirrored participant schedules are unimplemented.

replication_inputs.source_payloads: Obtain the original binaural recording, the constant-level baseline audio and the left/right conditioning source waveforms with checked provenance. The article's Open Practices statement on p. 1530 says the data and materials were not made public.
replication_inputs.output_check: Measure the headphone audio and all three actuator onsets against a common clock. Confirm that an active catch leaves both conditioning outputs playing and that a baseline disables both conditioning outputs. Record the transducers, routing, calibrated drive settings and measured onsets.
replication_inputs.order_and_scoring_check: Record the participant assignment and baseline placement, confirm that the second conditioning half reverses the first, and verify that numeric-keypad detection RT uses measured chest onset. The printed RT exclusions are offline.
replication_inputs.source: Published article, pp. 1523–1526 and 1530, Fig. 1, Methods, Analysis and Open Practices.

implementation_gaps: The exact binaural looming source and original left and right conditioning waveforms are unavailable. Absolute output levels, hardware calibration and timing from recorded sound onset are unreported.

A synchronized five-output scheduler needs independent left and right conditioning outputs, binaural playback and the chest target. The current three-role output map and its fourth-channel tactile duplicate cannot deliver those roles. Catch trials suppress only the chest target.
The trial scheduler needs a condition-specific block order with a reversed second half and a dedicated constant-level white-noise baseline with its own chest-target and catch trials.
Exact baseline trial allocation and catch counts by condition and block are unreported.
The response scheduler needs numeric-keypad capture timestamped relative to the chest target.
The exact accepted numeric key and online response deadline are unreported.
The exact individualized forearm-to-heel calibration staircase and practice settings are unreported.
